<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via createLink (symbol, a method of class ShareLinkService))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via createLink (symbol, a method of class ShareLinkService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 38 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `839bd9d94a680bf268681ceddb2b2834328b8585` — the merge of head `04c61e78e8bbf72cc36d704295c0e6670d59c87d` into base `276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 839bd9d94a680bf268681ceddb2b2834328b8585 && git checkout 839bd9d94a680bf268681ceddb2b2834328b8585
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1 04c61e78e8bbf72cc36d704295c0e6670d59c87d && git checkout -B drift-repro 276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1 && git merge --no-ff 04c61e78e8bbf72cc36d704295c0e6670d59c87d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 276ca307c5a1b2d9f83cd22c54edc14c1c1351c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `38ded5e5d522fa1001e1d691cc4edc389d1c07c3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-redact-fields.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/share-link-service.ts, packages/types/src/share-link-resolve-answer.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .changeset/29130-share-link-redact-fields.md (read for ②)

Reviewed read-only at 2026-11-02T11:31Z: the net diff `origin/main...38ded5e5`, card #29130 (body and every comment, claims 6573655861 and 6573762130 and the os-dev-report 6575674492 included), PR #29293 (body, file list), and the head's check-runs. Check-runs at posting: 48 on the head, all completed — 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure/neutral/cancelled (polled to completion before this record was written). The gate verdicts are green; the FAIL below is the record's own, on the declaration carrier.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/objectql`, entry `./core`** — gains one value export, `declaredColumnSet`, re-exported from `declared-read-columns.ts`. Read in the tree: `declared-read-columns.ts` already exports it and `engine.ts` consumes it at eight sites; `src/index.ts` does NOT re-publish `./core` (its only `core` lines are two `@objectstack/core` re-exports), so the widening lands on `./core` alone, as the PR and the revised claim state. **Right.** A widening of a published export; no type changes, no signature change.
- **REST accept set, `POST /api/v1/share-links` (and the dispatcher twin `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts`)** — `redactFields` is now refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when (a) it is not an array of strings, or (b) any entry is outside `declaredColumnSet(schema)`; both doors pass the body's `redactFields` straight to `createLink`, the REST door maps `err.status`/`err.code` via `sendError`, the dispatcher via `deps.errorFromThrown` (reads `status`), so both answer 400 with the existing envelope. **Right**: an input accepted `201` on `main` is refused on head — a NARROWING of a published accept set, exactly what the changeset's own prose says ("The mint now narrows").
- **Accept set kept** — omitted/`null`/`[]` still store `null`; names in the field map or in `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS` (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) are accepted; a schema with no checkable field map (absent, array, empty) returns `undefined` from `declaredColumnSet` and the list is stored as sent. **Right** — this is the shared rule of `declared-read-columns.ts` and the test pins each arm (`doc`, `bare`, `unmapped`).
- **Ordering** — the check sits after the visibility/A′ authority block and before `assertEligible`, so an unauthorised caller gets `403 FORBIDDEN` without learning column names. **Right**; pinned by the 403 test (`message` does not echo the name).
- **No new error code** — `VALIDATION_FAILED` already issued by this mint (`object is required`, `emailAllowlist is required…`). **Right.**
- **Stored rows** — untouched; `resolveToken`'s union `policy.redactFields ∪ row.redact_fields` unchanged. **Right**, and the residue is named in ③.
- **Ledger `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`** — two rows (`delete`, `update`, `pinned: 1`) for the new test file, inserted in the file's sort position (after `share-link-enforcement-context.test.ts`, before `sharing-rule-provenance.test.ts`), same shape as neighbours; the new double does call `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`/`assertEngineDeleteDispatch`. **The gate's output**, nothing else changed in the file.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: `patch` on both packages — right.** Under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3) the level follows `Metadata-protocol:` alone; this diff changes nothing a metadata author writes (`none`), so every entry is `patch`. A non-protocol widening or narrowing "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `skip-changeset` would be wrong (two released packages move); the changeset lists both. ✓
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.**
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — WRONG declaration for this diff. Must-fix (M1).** The one reader, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, spells out the four combinations: `yes`/`yes (widening)` = a widening; `no (narrowing)` = breaking, not a widening; and **`yes (narrowing)` — "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read."** This PR is that diff by its own account (and by the seat's original claim 6573655861, which read `no (narrowing)`). AGENTS.md allows "at most one arm", and the reader resolves which one carries when both are true: the `narrowing` arm, because it is the only carrier of the breaking signal here — the changeset has no `major`, no `**BREAKING**` banner and no `!`, so `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` signal (4) is the ONLY thing that can see this narrowing, and with `(widening)` it sees nothing and asks for no ADR-0087 disposition. That is the #16296 hole the arm was built to close, reopened by prose. `record-recognisers.mjs#reviewFace` reads the same arm: with the paths deciding no face, `yes (narrowing)` on any carrier ⇒ the narrowing face (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, ④ owed); `yes (widening)` ⇒ the declaration face (`TIER_DEFAULT`, no ④). So the line as written also under-routes the review the diff owes — the dispatching seat compensated by hand in this brief, but the committed carrier is what the queue guard reads. Prose ("The mint now narrows") is not read by any gate.
  **Fix**: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/29130-share-link-redact-fields.md`; then, because the changeset declares breaking, exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker in its body (the HTML-comment form `adr-0087: not-required (CATEGORY) WHY`, category from the gate's own print — no spec key moves and no migration ledger entry applies) and the migration line AGENTS.md asks of a breaking changeset (the FROM→TO is already in prose: "correct the name, or drop it" — keep it, under a `**BREAKING**` banner). Level stays `patch`.
- Changeset body otherwise follows the diff: both packages, the narrowing stated, the unchanged set stated, stored rows stated, the new `./core` export named. ✓

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the claim's file surface** — accepted. Gate-forced coverage ledger, judged in ① as the gate's output. Not a shrink-only baseline.
- **Deviation: `Clause-②` copied as `yes (widening)` per revised claim 6573762130** — ⛔ not accepted; see ② M1. The revised claim's instruction to put the narrowing "in the PR body" as prose contradicts the reader it must satisfy. The seat ruling on the single-source route (re-export `declaredColumnSet`) stands; the declaration spelling does not.
- **Deviation: closure build rerun with `--workspace-concurrency=2`** — process note, nothing to judge.
- **Open question 1 (stored rows still list an unknown name at resolve; filter?)** — A (this PR) agreed. B (display-only filter in `@objectstack/types` `buildShareLinkResolveAnswer`) is a separate card on a types surface; C (filter the effective set in `resolveToken`) is rightly refused — the same list drives redaction and a gap in the column set would un-hide a policy entry. Escalation: file B as a follow-up card; not a condition of this PR.
- **Open question 2 (no checkable field map ⇒ no verdict; fail closed instead?)** — A agreed. It is `declaredColumnSet`'s shared rule on every read/write door, and a non-system, non-permissive caller is refused `422 SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` before the check when `getSchema` answers nothing (read: `getPolicy(undefined)` ⇒ `enabled: false`). Only `permissive`/system callers reach the mint without a schema, and those bypass the policy by design (system-context ledger row 38).
- **Open question 3 (system columns; update path)** — as implemented: provisioned columns accepted exactly when `declaredColumnSet` holds them; no update/edit verb exists for a link's `redactFields` (create/list/revoke/resolve only, read in `share-link-routes.ts` and the dispatcher), so the mint is the only entry.
- **Docs drift advisory** (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 38 names `createLink`) — read: the row describes the system-context bypass of the `enabled` check, which this diff does not touch; nothing falsified. `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx` is release-owned and untouched. ✓
- **Dogfood battery** — n/a per the report (no `!` in title). Note: once M1 lands as `yes (narrowing)`, re-read whether the dev-report's dogfood clause (`Clause-② arm is (widening)`) still exempts the PR; the targeted share-link dogfood files already ran 41/41.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts`** — holds against the cited code and the card's scenario.
- `assertRedactFields` judges against `declaredColumnSet(schema)` where `schema = this.engine.getSchema?.(input.object)` — the same registry object `resolveToken` reads for its policy and the same set the engine shapes rows to on every read (`engine.ts` `find`/`findOne`/`insert`/`update`/`delete` sites), so "a name is accepted exactly when the read serves a column by that name" is true for storage-backed columns. The card's repro (`sumary` ⇒ 201 ⇒ served in full under a "hidden" notice) now ends at the mint with 400 and no row. ✓
- Break attempts: `''` and whitespace names are refused (not in the set) ✓; duplicates in a valid list are stored as sent (pre-existing; harmless, resolve builds a `Set`) ✓; `internal: true` fields are declared and so redactable (harmless — already omitted by the read) ✓; a name present only in the object policy's `redactFields` is not consulted (right — the per-link list is the input under judgment; the policy list is an authoring question outside this card) ✓; `permissive` mode with no schema ⇒ no verdict, list kept (the shared rule; ③ Q2) ✓; the refusal message names only the unknown entries, deduplicated, and nothing about valid ones (pinned) ✓.
- **Residual edge (observation, no finding):** a key the served record carries that the field map does not declare — one an `afterFind` hook or `expand` adds after the engine's declared-column shaping — was redactable on `main` (the name matched a served key) and is now refused as "does not have". `declared-read-columns.ts` names such keys as "the engine's or the hook's, not storage's". The mint's rule is the right one for the card (a name must have a column behind it); the docblock's "exactly when there is something for it to hide" is one notch stronger than the code. No change asked.
- **Should-fix (S1):** the request-SHAPE half of the check (`Array.isArray` / `typeof name === 'string'`) runs after the authority read, unlike the mint's other 400 request-shape checks (`object`, `recordId`, `emailAllowlist`), which run before any DB read. Only the COLUMN half needs the authority ordering (it is what leaks column names). Splitting the shape check up to the request-shape block keeps a malformed body from paying a record read and keeps the mint's own 400-before-403 convention for shape; the 403-first test stays true because it sends a well-shaped list. Not a FAIL on its own.

**`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`** — holds. One value re-export, source already exported from its module and already consumed by `engine.ts`; comment states the consumer and the single-list reason. `./core` is the lean entry, `index.ts` does not fan it out, so the widening is exactly the one declared. ✓

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-redact-fields.test.ts`** — holds against the scenario. Fixtures shaped like the registry's (`id` outside the field map; `bare` carries no timestamps in the map) so the provisioned-column arm is really exercised; every refusal pinned on `status` + `code` + row-count, no bare `toThrow()`; the 403-ordering case checks the name is not echoed; the REST case mounts the real `registerShareLinkRoutes` and reads the envelope (`success: false`, `error.code`). The double pins `update`/`delete` to the engine's dispatch contract, honours `limit` and refuses `$` combinators — what the three gates asked. The mixed case asserts the `bdoy, titel` ordering and dedup against the message spelling in the service, which is the right pin for "names every unknown entry once". ✓

**`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`** — the gate's output (①), judged only as such. ✓

Findings: **M1** (must-fix) — `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the wrong carrier for a diff that widens `./core` AND narrows the share-link mint; spell `yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset and add the ADR-0087 disposition marker the gate then requires (level stays `patch`). **S1** (should-fix) — move the array-of-strings shape check of `redactFields` before the record read, beside the mint's other request-shape 400s.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gor7h6`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQjPiXgNoSaEpqeGvY`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `04c61e78e8bbf72cc36d704295c0e6670d59c87d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-redact-fields.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/share-link-service.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .changeset/29130-share-link-redact-fields.md (read for ②)

Round 2, rendered read-only at 2026-11-02T12:41Z. Supersedes record 6576071712 (FAIL, on head `38ded5e5`). Inputs: the round-2 delta `38ded5e5..04c61e78` (one commit), the net diff `origin/main...04c61e78`, card #29130 with every comment (the round-2 os-dev-report 6577314563 included), the PR body as rewritten at 2026-11-02T12:38Z, and the head's check-runs. Check-runs at posting: 52 on the head, all completed — 37 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure/neutral/cancelled, none still in progress (polled to completion before this record was written). The gate verdicts are green, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` included.

### ① Derived judgments

Re-read on the WHOLE net diff; the delta touches no accept set or public surface beyond moving one check earlier.

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/objectql` entry `./core`** — unchanged since round 1: one value export `declaredColumnSet`, `index.ts` does not fan `./core` out. **Right.**
- **REST accept set, `POST /api/v1/share-links` and the dispatcher twin** — `redactFields` refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when (a) not an array of strings or (b) an entry is outside `declaredColumnSet(schema)`. Delta: (a) now runs in the request-shape block (after the `emailAllowlist` check, before `readRecord`), (b) stays after the authority block and before `assertEligible`. Same codes, same envelope, same stored row; the accept set is byte-for-byte the one round 1 judged. **Right** — a narrowing of a published accept set, now declared as such (②).
- **Ordering consequence of the delta** — a malformed `redactFields` from a caller with no authority now answers 400 instead of 403. The shape refusal reveals nothing about the object or the record (it is a statement about the request body alone), so the 403-before-anything rule that guards column names is intact; the column check is still 403-first and the test pins it. **Right.**
- **Accept set kept** — omitted/`null`/`[]` ⇒ `null` stored; provisioned columns accepted; uncheckable field map ⇒ no verdict (`assertRedactFieldColumns` also returns at once on an empty list, so an empty list never consults the schema). **Right.**
- **Ledger** — unchanged since round 1, the gate's output. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **M1 — RESOLVED.** `.changeset/29130-share-link-redact-fields.md` at the head and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset carries a `**BREAKING**:` banner that names the door, the old and new answers and the FROM → TO fix (correct the name, or drop the entry), and EXACTLY ONE ADR-0087 disposition marker in the HTML-comment form the gate reads, category `no-migration-prescription` (one of the gate's `CATEGORIES`), with a reason that is true of the tree: no metadata key, spec schema or stored row moves, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. Read against `clause2-line.mjs`: `yes (narrowing)` is the spelling for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads signals BREAKING and clause-②-narrowing and finds the disposition; `reviewFace` now routes the PR to the narrowing face (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, ④ owed) — the face this record serves.
- **Level: `patch` on both packages — right** (ruling A: the level follows `Metadata-protocol:` alone; `none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition, which it now does). `skip-changeset` would be wrong; both released packages are listed.
- Changeset body follows the diff: narrowing stated, unchanged set stated, stored rows stated, the `./core` export named. The round-2 placement of the shape check is covered by the existing "A `redactFields` that is not an array of strings answers the same" sentence (the status and code did not change, only where it is asked). ✓

### ③ Boundary flags

- **M1 / S1 round-2 deviations** — the dev reports the commit was amended once locally before push (no pushed history rewritten) and that the ADR-0087 marker is an HTML comment in the changeset file (the form the gate requires, invisible in a published changelog by design). Both accepted.
- **Deviation: ledger outside the claim's file surface** — accepted, as in round 1.
- **Open questions 1–3** — unchanged from round 1 and answered there: Q1 A now, B (display-only filter in `@objectstack/types` `buildShareLinkResolveAnswer`) as a follow-up card, C refused; Q2 A (the shared `declaredColumnSet` rule; a non-system, non-permissive caller is refused `422 SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` before the check when no schema answers); Q3 as implemented. Nothing in the delta reopens them.
- **Dogfood battery** — the dev ran the full battery under the `(narrowing)` arm (388 files / 3208 tests passed, 0 failures, per report 6577314563); not re-run here, the check-runs are the gate verdicts.
- **PR body prose nit (not reviewed, noted)** — the 「先看」 bullet still names `assertRedactFields`, a function the delta split into `redactFieldsShape` and `assertRedactFieldColumns`; the English sections describe the two-step shape correctly. Prose only; the seat holding the body may refresh it.
- **Docs drift advisory** — same two pages as round 1 (`system-context.mdx` row 38 and the release-owned `v14.mdx`); the delta changes nothing they state.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts`** — holds; **S1 — RESOLVED.**
